context.projectOverview: Close every conformance divergence and run every graph node — The graph engine is built but not finished: four conformance fields still diverge from the imperative pipeline, and six of its nodes have never executed in any run. This spec closes all four divergences at their architectural causes and drives all six nodes to execution, so the flip bar becomes satisfiable as originally written. The default stays 'ts' — this makes the flip a decision you can take with evidence, not a risk this spec takes.

completedSprints.title: Checkpoints inside the sprint fan-out — the ADR decision
completedSprints.summary: Revisited ADR-6 and concluded the InterruptInsideFanOut rule STANDS, now for a runtime-grounded reason ADR-6 never gave: Checkpoint.interrupt is a single slot (checkpointer.ts:247); grantScope has no branch key and clearScope evicts by prefix (interrupt.ts:268,371-375,485); resumeMessageId has no branch key so N decisions collapse to one message row (:332, plan.ts:142-144). New ADR arch-20260814-pge-full-convergence-adr-1. CONSEQUENCE: five of six undeclared checkpoint ids stay permanently undeclarable, so audits cannot fully converge — spec feat-1 and feat-3 were amended to record that. NO interrupt mechanics were changed (interrupt.ts/checkpointer.ts/interpreter.ts diffs are empty) — that is THIS sprint's territory.

contract.title: Gated effects execute under a durable approval
contract.description: `commit` and `finalize` have never executed: noop grants nothing and nothing in this repo ever runs them under another mechanism, so commit's span is always interrupted/FailClosed. Give them a durable approval path so their bodies actually run.

successCriteria.description: A run supplied with a durable approval record executes the commit node's body: its span status is 'ok', not 'interrupted' with errorClass FailClosed.
Fail-closed is NOT weakened: with no approval record present, the effect is still refused. Pinned by a test that fails if the guard is removed.
commit and finalize are removed from NEVER_EXECUTED (src/pge/golden/coverage.test.ts:139-146) and the list's two-directional guard still fails if a node silently re-enters it.
The approval record is durable in the sense interrupt.ts:38-46 means — it survives process exit and is not synthesised by the harness at run time.
Every golden case whose recorded artifacts move is re-captured in THIS sprint, with each diff hunk read and confined to the newly-executing nodes and their direct consequences.
Full suite, typecheck, typecheck:tests, lint and build green, and the golden gate passing at or above its replay floor.

nonGoals: Changing deriveRunSuccess or the completion marker — Option A stays frozen.
stopConditions: Making commit execute requires the golden executor to stop pinning one config, which would make cases irreproducible — stop and report rather than trading reproducibility for coverage.
contract.definitionOfDone: All required criteria met, the full suite plus typecheck, typecheck:tests, lint and build green, the golden gate passing, and every documentation claim added backed by a test that fails when the claim stops being true.
contract.generatorNotes: Four mechanisms are registered at src/pge/runtime/interrupt.ts:318 (cli, disk, pr, noop); `disk` is the obvious durable one. The grant rule is :523 `if (mechanismName !== "noop") granted.set(key, outcome)`. The shipped conformanceConfig() is autopilot by construction and the golden executor pins it deliberately so cases reproduce — do NOT unpin that. The likely shape is a second, explicitly-approved config used by new cases, leaving the autopilot path exactly as it is. commit is a git-effect node: make sure executing it in a test cannot touch the real repo. Run the suite as `npx vitest run --exclude '**/.claude/worktrees/**' --exclude '**/node_modules/**'` — a bare run picks up nested worktrees. principles:
# Project Principles

> These principles guide all planning, generation, and evaluation in the Bober pipeline.
> Updated: 2026-04-16

## Mission

Agent-bober is a multi-agent harness that builds applications autonomously using any LLM. It orchestrates a pipeline of specialized agents (Researcher, Planner, Curator, Generator, Evaluator) and supports Claude, GPT, Gemini, and Ollama. It ships as an npm CLI + MCP server for Claude Code, Cursor, and Windsurf.

## Users

- **Primary:** Developers using Claude Code, Cursor, or Windsurf who want autonomous feature generation with quality gates
- **Secondary:** Teams integrating agent-bober programmatically via the TypeScript API or MCP server
- Technical level: intermediate to advanced — users understand LLMs, CI/CD, and modern JS tooling

## Quality Standards

- **Type safety:** TypeScript strict mode with all strict flags (`noUnusedLocals`, `noUnusedParameters`, `noImplicitReturns`, `noFallthroughCasesInSwitch`, `isolatedModules`). Zero type errors is a hard gate.
- **Lint compliance:** ESLint flat config with `consistent-type-imports` enforced, `no-explicit-any` warned, unused vars errored (with `_` prefix escape). Zero lint errors is a hard gate.
- **Test coverage:** Vitest for unit tests. Tests are collocated with source (`*.test.ts` next to `*.ts`). Tests run against the real project when practical (e.g., scanner tests scan agent-bober itself).
- **Build integrity:** `tsc` must produce clean output. Build is a required evaluator strategy.

## Technical Principles

### Follow

- **ESM everywhere.** `"type": "module"` in package.json. All imports use `.js` extensions for NodeNext resolution. No CommonJS.
- **Provider-agnostic interfaces.** All LLM interaction goes through `providers/types.ts` — provider-specific SDKs are wrapped by adapters (`anthropic.ts`, `openai.ts`, `google.ts`). Never leak SDK types outside adapter files.
- **Zod for config validation.** All configuration schemas are Zod schemas in `config/schema.ts`. Runtime config loading uses `z.parse()`. No hand-rolled validation.
- **Contract-based architecture.** PlanSpecs, SprintContracts, and EvalResults are the communication protocol between agents. They live in `contracts/` and are JSON files on disk in `.bober/`.
- **Filesystem state.** All mutable state (specs, contracts, handoffs, eval results, history) is stored as JSON files in `.bober/`. No database, no in-memory global state.
- **Section comments.** Use unicode box-drawing section headers: `// -- Section Name ------` to organize long files.
- **Small utility modules.** Utils in `utils/` are focused single-purpose files (`fs.ts`, `git.ts`, `logger.ts`). Keep them small.
- **Conventional commits.** Format: `type: description` where type is `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `release`, `refactor`, `test`, `chore`. Sprint-generated commits use `bober(sprint-N): description`.
- **Use `type` imports.** ESLint enforces `consistent-type-imports` -- import types with `import type { ... }` syntax.
- **Prefix unused params with `_`.** The `_` prefix is the only escape hatch for unused variables/parameters.

### Avoid

- **No `any` without justification.** `no-explicit-any` is a warning; aim for zero. Use `unknown` + type narrowing instead.
- **No SDK lock-in.** Never import `@anthropic-ai/sdk` or `openai` outside of their respective adapter files in `providers/`.
- **No synchronous filesystem ops.** All fs operations use `node:fs/promises`. No `fs.readFileSync` etc.
- **No barrel re-exports for deep internals.** `src/index.ts` exports the public API only. Internal modules import directly.
- **No test mocks for filesystem.** Tests that need filesystem state create temp directories and clean up. The scanner tests run against the real codebase.

## Design Principles

N/A -- no user interface. Agent-bober is a CLI tool and programmatic library. The MCP server exposes tools, not UI.
